questions.q: What does a Gauge data region display?
options: A single aggregated value from a dataset
An entire series of data points over time
Every row of the underlying dataset, unaggregated
Only text-based KPI labels, never numbers
questions.explain: A gauge distills a dataset down to one value and shows where it falls inside a defined range — unlike a chart, which plots a whole series.

questions.q: What container must every gauge be positioned inside?
options: A gauge panel
A matrix
A parameter group
A shared dataset
questions.explain: Every gauge lives inside a gauge panel, the top-level container that can hold one or more gauges (or indicators) sharing filtering, grouping, and sorting.

questions.q: What's the key visual and structural difference between a radial and a linear gauge?
options: Radial gauges are circular with needle-style pointers; linear gauges are rectangular with thermometer-style pointers
Radial gauges only show whole numbers; linear gauges only show percentages
Linear gauges cannot be placed inside a table cell
There is no real difference — they render identically
questions.explain: Radial gauges are circular, resembling a speedometer with a needle; linear gauges are rectangular, resembling a ruler with a thermometer-style pointer, which makes them easy to fit inside table or matrix cells.

questions.q: Which aggregate function does a gauge use by default for a numeric field?
options: SUM
AVERAGE
COUNT
MAX
questions.explain: Numeric fields dragged onto a gauge are aggregated with SUM by default; non-numeric fields use COUNT instead.

questions.q: What will Reporting Services NOT do automatically when you add data to a gauge?
options: Set the scale's minimum and maximum values
Attach the aggregated value to the pointer
Create a pointer if one doesn't already exist
Bind the field using SUM or COUNT
questions.explain: The gauge will not set the scale's minimum and maximum for you — it has no way to know what "full" should mean for your specific data, so you must set those explicitly.
